[its own changelog](https://github.com/VeriWorkly/ats-engine/blob/main/packages/mcp/CHANGELOG.md).

## 0.22.0

### Minor Changes

- 03c88f8: PDF reading no longer decodes an image of more than 4096 × 4096 pixels (about a letter page scanned at 400 dpi). A crafted PDF of a few huge images used to make the reader allocate gigabytes of pixels outside V8's heap, enough to have the process killed. pdf.js now leaves such an image undrawn, so in a PDF that has one, the image and hidden-text signals (`imageOnlyPages`, `imageCount`, `hiddenTextChars`) are reported as not measured rather than read from a page missing its picture: a 600 dpi scan is not called a blank page, and its OCR layer is not called hidden text. PDFs without such an image read exactly as before.

## 0.21.0

### Minor Changes

- 4888dab: The 2026-10-22 full-repo audit's 64 open findings are fixed. Each fix has a test that failed before it, and the hidden-text and HTML changes were checked on real files: 38 PDFs and Word documents made with Chrome, Word and published resume themes (banners, sidebars, photos, icons, text boxes, watermarks, shaded tables) read exactly as in 0.20.0 with no hidden text, real covers are found, and 38 real job postings and careers pages read word for word as before. English resumes read as in 0.20.0: on 1,089 runs (every English fixture, 300 generated resumes, the private graded set and review cases, alone and with postings), no score, matched keyword or requirement status changes; requirement evidence now quotes a line with its column gap as one space. The bench lists no miss, in every language and format.

  - **Breaking, hidden text:** a structured resume's invisible characters are counted on its fields as given, so tag characters in a JSON Resume are flagged as they are in text. A Word file's headers, footers and embedded pages are read only where a section or the body places them; its alternate content is measured as Word shows it; text hidden by a character or paragraph style, white or two-point text, or text squashed to a sliver is hidden. A PDF's text in a layer the file turns off is hidden, as is the part of a line a box drawn over it covers, and only that part, wherever the box sits (a box over half a bullet hid the whole bullet and its visible keywords); ruled tables are counted on a crowded page; a soft mask is checked within a fixed budget (24,000 glyphs under 24,000 paints: 15 s before, under 2 s now). An HTML resume's text hidden by a style sheet class or written near-white on no background is hidden, unless another of its classes shows it on some screen or in some state (utility classes such as "hidden lg:flex", a menu opened on hover) or it sits in the page's navigation or footer, which are a site's, not a resume's; and a self-closed hiding tag ("<span hidden/>") hides what follows, as a browser reads it. Hidden lines are left out of the job match even below the hidden-text rule's threshold (three hidden keywords no longer lift a match from 25 to 100).
  - **Breaking, parsing:** role headers written as bullets ("- Senior Engineer, Globex Corp — Jan 2021 – Present") are roles when no other line is dated; several titles under one employer's line each keep it; ordinal days ("1st Jan 2020"), an arrow ("May 2019 → Present") and two-digit or season dates in structured input are read; LinkedIn's certification rows (name, issuer, "Issued … · Expires …") are one row, "PMP, CSM, CISSP" three, and an inactive one is "partial" against a requirement; a lowercase description is never joined onto its dated header; "Work Experiences", "Career History" and "Positions Held" are experience headings, and "History Teacher" is a title; phone numbers printed with en dashes are read; a role's span counts no month after today; links keep their own brackets and commas; an education entry's dates on a line of their own end it. A document naming another version of the structured format ("ats-resume@2") is an `AtsInputError`, not text.
  - **Breaking, languages and policy:** an English resume with no bullets is weighed whole, so place names ("Des Moines", "Les Schwab") no longer read it as French; "a level 2 support role", "computer literate", "sales promotion" and "Certificate of Sponsorship" ask for no degree; a language row stating two levels reads the higher. A policy is refused, with the path, when a years or language pattern has no capturing group, a synonym's key has a space, or a region pack's rule id is one or two letters off a real one ("did you mean …"); other unknown rule ids are still ignored. Language names in a pack match in any case, seniority level names too. The fingerprint now covers the detection words of the packs a resume is read in. `check` no longer freezes a host's own unparsed policy.
  - **Breaking, matching and scoring:** "AWS or Google Cloud" is two alternatives; a posting's structured qualifications and responsibilities are read under their own headings; requirement lines copied into a resume fail the copied-posting check; the words of a link's path and of the contact line are no keywords; short tools ("dbt", "git", "npm") are judged; a product named after a tool the policy knows ("Apache Pulsar") stays; a list repeating one term inside Experience is stuffing, a role's own "Technologies:" line is not; a twice-escaped posting is unescaped; "Resume.final" is advised as a draft. The report says when a resume was cut at 50,000 characters or a posting's requirements past the 25th were not judged, and gains `keywordCounts` (`matched`, `missing`), which a restricted report's counts use past twelve.
  - **Breaking, AI:** `repairParse` reports a reply that fills no field the parse left empty, because it gave none or only values not in the resume or already parsed, as an `AtsAiError` with the new code `unusable`, instead of returning the parse unchanged as repaired. It is not retried (asked again, a model rarely finds more, and each attempt is billed) and carries `usage`, `attempts` and the dropped values in `rejected`. `runAiEval` reports it as `unusableRate`.
  - **AI and CLI:** the `--ai` notice promises to hide only the contact details the parser read; `convertResume` drops an entry whose every identity value was invented; a suggestion's opening claim is checked unless it is an instruction verb; repair keeps a month only where the document writes it ("2019 - 2022" stays 48 months); an email glued to a dash is grounded; grounding thousands of values is fast; an HTTP 200 reply that is a JSON list is not retried; a UTF-8 file with a byte-order mark is never read as Windows-1252; the reader's child process reports the reader's own error and answers a malformed request.
  - **Development:** `npm test` never runs the paid live eval (`npm run eval:live` has its own config), and `npm run test:private` runs the private-policy tests before a release (CONTRIBUTING). The GitHub Action stops the engine and every process it started at its time limit, and its README says to pin a `version` or a commit.
  - The default policy's fingerprint is `ats-v2+6e295cb1` in this release. Bundles (gzip): `.` 115.2 KB, `./locales` 92.4 KB, `./ai` 81.1 KB, `./node` 25.7 KB, `./job` 4.5 KB.

- a75165a: Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Chile are read as their own regions, every pack is corrected by a linguist's review, and every miss the bench still listed is read right.

  Measured against 0.20.0 on the resumes an independent reviewer wrote for each language (text, DOCX and PDF; detected and with the language given alike): German 99.2% to 100%, Hindi 99.2% to 100%, Spanish 99.3% to 100%, Portuguese 99.3% to 100%, French 100%. No field is read worse. `npm run bench` now also reads every language as a PDF in a Unicode font, and `bench/baseline.json` lists no miss at all: every hand-written resume and every generated one, in English as text, PDF, two-column PDF and DOCX, and in German, French, Hindi, Spanish and Portuguese as text, DOCX and PDF, is read in full. English: on 1,089 runs (every English fixture, 300 generated resumes, the private graded set, review cases, alone and with postings), one resume differs from 0.20.0: its B.Com is read at level 6.

  - **Breaking:** new region packs `MX`, `AR`, `CO` and `CL`, all `community`. Each reads its national phone numbers, its state codes after a city ("Monterrey, N.L.", "Santiago, RM", "Bogotá D.C."), its cities, and its schooling: preparatoria (3) and TSU (5) in Mexico; secundario (3) and tecnicatura (5) in Argentina; bachiller (3), técnico profesional and tecnólogo (5) in Colombia; enseñanza media (3) and técnico de nivel superior (5) in Chile. CABA and CDMX are the cities themselves, so "Arcor, CABA" reads employer "Arcor". A date of birth or a photo is not judged there. In 0.20.0 such a resume took Spain's region: an Argentine or Colombian number without its country code went unread.
  - **Breaking:** for a resume a language pack reads, the region also comes from its header when the phone has no country code: an email's or site's country domain ("@empresa.com.ar", ".cl"; never ".co" alone, which startups use), else the country's name or one of its cities ("Buenos Aires, Argentina", "Lisboa"). The header ends after the contact line, so a role's city never names it. An English resume is left to its phone number, as before.
  - **Breaking:** an honorific before the name is not part of it: "Dr. Miriam Hoffmann", "Prof. Dr. med. Anna Schmidt", "Lic. Ana Ramírez", "Dra. Inês Sousa", "Mme Claire Martin" and "डॉ. अंजलि मिश्रा" read the name alone. A new policy field, `namePrefixes` (English: Dr, Prof, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx; each pack adds its own). It is cut only while two name words remain, and undotted capitals are initials ("MS Dhoni" stays).
  - **Breaking:** a resume repeats one layout. Once one role reads "Cargo en Empresa S.L." (Spanish "en", Portuguese "na", "no", "em" before a legal form), every role is read that way, the last such word before a comma parting title from employer: "Especialista en Marketing en Cielo Azul Software" reads title "Especialista en Marketing", employer "Cielo Azul Software". A new pack field, `layoutEmployerWords`. Without such a role, "Especialista en Marketing" stays a title.
  - **Breaking:** a city beside a role's dates, with the employer and title stacked above it ("Paris 04/2024 à aujourd'hui"), is where the role is worked, not the employer. A city alone with no header above may still be the employer ("Santander").
  - **Breaking:** in a PDF, a short run flush with the right margin is a tab stop even without a digit, when at least two in five such lines hold dates: a city on the employer's line over the dates on the title's ("Sahyadri Systems Ltd … पुणे" over "Analyst … 2019 – 2022") is no longer read as a second column, which had cut those roles from their dates.
  - **Breaking:** schools and credentials. Fundação Getulio Vargas and Colombia's "Fundación Universitaria" and "Corporación Universitaria" are schools; an institution named by its word alone beside a credential is the school ("Tecnólogo en Logística, SENA, 2013", "INACAP"). B.Com and M.Com are read with no region (Australia, South Africa and Ireland write them too). "BUT Informatique" reads credential "BUT", its speciality the field, as "Diplôme d'ingénieur en Génie logiciel" reads "Diplôme d'ingénieur". "Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker" keeps its occupation. Portuguese reads "administrador", "gestor", "executivo", "operador", "representante", "secretário", "médico" and "advogado" as titles.
  - **Breaking:** a program named by its field alone before a university is the first degree in Spanish and Portuguese, where postgraduate and technologist programs always name themselves: "Administración de Empresas, Universidad de Antioquia" reads level 6. A new pack field, `universityWords` ("universidad", "universidade"); English sets none, so "Computer Science, Stanford University" still reads no level. Spanish "Tecnología en …" and "Técnico Superior/Profesional" read level 5 in any region.
  - **Breaking:** a linguist's review of every language and region pack (not a native speaker's sign-off: every pack stays `community`), each finding tested:
    - Hindi: "5 वर्षों का अनुभव" in a posting is a years requirement; "प्रमाण पत्र", "शैक्षणिक योग्यताएँ", "प्रमुख कौशल", "घोषणा" and "व्यक्तिगत जानकारी" are headings; "10वीं", "12वीं", "इण्टरमीडिएट", "उच्च माध्यमिक", "बी.एड", "बी.एस.सी.", "पी.एच.डी.", "एम.फिल", ITI and diplomas (4) are read; "नाम:" labels the name; Hindi-belt cities, Indian states and twelve more titles ("अभियंता", "लेखाकार", "अध्यापक"). In India, "10+2", "Xth" and "Matric" are read and "Graduated 12th May" is no Class XII.
    - Spanish: "Jefe de Proyectos" and every "Jefe de/del …" is a title; "S.A.U." and undotted "SA de CV" mark an employer; LinkedIn's levels ("Competencia bilingüe o nativa" C2) and "nivel medio" (B1) are read; Chile's "Antecedentes laborales", Mexico's "Escolaridad" are headings; Spain's "Graduado en", "Diplomatura" and "Ingeniería Técnica" are degrees, while an Argentine "Diplomatura" read in Argentina (an extension course) and a Latin American "Diplomado" (a course) are none; a role "Ingeniero en Sistemas" keeps its field, and a header naming "España" is Spain whatever city it names; Argentina's "Profesorado" (6), Chile's "4° Medio" (3). "desde", "mediante" and "académica" no longer count as Spanish, since Portuguese writes them too.
    - Portuguese: "Bacharelato", "Doutoramento", Portugal's "Habilitações Literárias" and "Percurso profissional", "até à data", "actual", "cursando", "S/A", LinkedIn's "Proficiência profissional" levels, and Brazil's "2º grau" are read.
    - German: Swiss "fliessend"; Austria's and Switzerland's Matura, Berufsmaturität and EFZ (3); "Dipl.-Ing. FH" and Swiss "dipl. … HF" at level 6, not 7; "Berufliche Erfahrungen", "Praktika", "PC-Kenntnisse" and "Zusatzqualifikationen" as headings; "Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter", "Fachkraft", "Industriekaufmann" as titles; AG, KG and e. V. mark an employer; "Mag.a" and "Ing." before a name.
    - French: "chef d'équipe" (the pack said "chef de équipe"), "Président", "Chercheur", "Professeur"; LinkedIn's levels ("Capacité professionnelle complète" C2); "brevet de technicien supérieur" (5), while BAFA is no brevet des collèges; Switzerland's maturité and CFC and Belgium's CESS and "bachelier en"; "Licences et certifications", "Scolarité", "Vie associative" as headings; "jusqu'à ce jour".
  - **Breaking:** a line that opens with "| " goes on with a piped line the page wrapped ("PMP | PMI | Issued Jan 2024" over "| Expires Jan 2027"); a Markdown table row, which ends in "|", is not joined.
  - The default policy's fingerprint changes in this release; the bundle sizes are in the audit fixes' note.

- a75165a: A resume in a language no pack reads can be read with AI help: step 5 of the language plan.

  - `ats-engine check --ai` on a resume the engine names as unsupported (Italian, Dutch, Russian, Japanese…) first sends the whole resume, contact details included, to the model you choose, which returns its fields (`convertResume`). Every name, employer, title, school, skill, email and link must appear in the file, or it is dropped, and so must every bullet and summary before it is scored (`groundedText`), so a bullet the model wrote, or one text planted in the resume steered it to write, adds no keyword; the engine then scores what is left as a structured document, and the analysis runs on that report. The output says "Read with AI help" above the report, and `--json` adds `readWithAi` (provider, model, language, values dropped). If the model fails, the engine's own reading stands and the exit code is 1. An English, German, French, Hindi, Spanish or Portuguese resume is read as before.
  - New in `/ai`: `groundedText(result, source)` blanks the summaries and bullets of a `convertResume` result that do not occur in the source, and `convertedToDocument(result)` turns a `convertResume` result into an `ats-resume@1` document for `check`. An entry whose identifying fields were all blanked as ungrounded is dropped, never scored on its bullets alone.
  - `check` accepts in `languages` a language the policy recognises but no pack reads (`text.otherLanguages`, by id or script: "it", "Cyrillic"), and reads the resume as detection would: no pack, the English writing rules off. The AI reading scores its document so, keeping its bullets from the English rules.
  - The base degrees read Italian, Polish, Russian, Swedish and Dutch degree names ("Laurea" 6, "Laurea magistrale" 7, "Бакалавр" 6, "Магистр" 7, "Licencjat" 6, "Dottorato" 8, "Matura" 3).
  - Each of `text.otherLanguages` gains `openEnded`, its words for a role still held ("oggi", "heden", "obecnie", "настоящее время", "至今"), so a model's "current" for such a resume is checked against the file as it is for a pack's language.
  - The CLI's AI error messages name the request, not only the analysis ("did not return a usable answer").

## 0.20.0

### Minor Changes

- c3a0d31: A resume in a language the engine has no pack for now says so, instead of a lower score with no reason.

  - **Breaking:** `report.locale` gains `unsupported`: the language a resume is written in when the policy recognises it (`text.otherLanguages`) and no pack read for it is that language, as an ISO 639 code (`"it"`, `"ja"`), a script the policy names no single language for (`"Cyrillic"`), or `"und"` for an entry of words alone; `null` otherwise. `parsingWarnings` gets the matching line: "This resume looks Italian, which the engine does not read yet: section names, dates and degrees were read as English, and the English writing checks were skipped." Such a resume was already read that way, silently; this line changes no score or field (21,402 runs over the fixtures, the private graded resumes, the review cases and 300 generated resumes, with and without packs, options and postings, were the same apart from it). With the built-in packs attached, only the Italian and Russian test resumes get it; with no pack attached (`check(text)` on `DEFAULT_POLICY`) a German, French or Hindi resume gets it too, since nothing reads those languages then: attach `BUILT_IN_LOCALES` with `withLocales`.
  - **Breaking:** the policy's `text.otherLanguages` entries take an optional `id`, an ISO 639 code. The default policy names its eight word lists (es, pt, it, fr, de, nl, pl, sv) and the scripts one language writes (Greek el, Hebrew he, Japanese kana ja, Hangul ko, Thai th, Tamil ta, Telugu te), and checks Japanese kana before Han, so a Japanese resume is named Japanese rather than by the Han script it shares with Chinese. An entry whose `id` is the policy's own language, or "und", is skipped, so a German-language policy that keeps the default list no longer reads German resumes in "und". The default policy's fingerprint changes; its value in this release is in the next entry.
  - The CLI prints the line under "Read as", once, with or without a posting; the MCP text answer and the GitHub Action's summary print it too.

- c3a0d31: German, French and Hindi resumes read nearly as well as English ones, and Spanish and Portuguese are read too.

  Measured against 0.19.0 on resumes an independent reviewer wrote for each language (its own layouts and labels: stacked, employer-first, dates first, pipe tables, LinkedIn exports, all-caps headings), read as text, DOCX and PDF alike, with the language detected:

  | Language   | 0.19.0 | 0.20.0 |
  | ---------- | ------ | ------ |
  | German     | 80.0%  | 99.2%  |
  | French     | 89.8%  | 97.6%  |
  | Hindi      | 88.4%  | 99.2%  |
  | Spanish    | 24.3%  | 98.0%  |
  | Portuguese | 23.3%  | 99.3%  |

  No field any of them read right in 0.19.0 is read wrong now, and passing the language (`--lang`, `language`) gives the same. `npm run bench` now also measures 30 generated resumes in each of the five languages and fails on any new miss. English: on 1,089 runs (every English fixture, 300 generated resumes, the private graded set, review cases, alone and with postings) only the changes below differ from 0.19.0, each one a field read better.

  - **Breaking:** a city after the employer is where the role is worked (decision D1): "Firma GmbH, Berlin", "Deutsche Bank, Frankfurt", "Infosys — Bengaluru" and "Thar Insurance, चेन्नई" read the employer alone. The cities are data, a new pack field `cityNames` that every built-in language and region pack fills, leaving out names that are also words or employers ("Nice", "Reading", "Phoenix"). With no region known, every attached region's cities are read; the base policy names none. A line that is only a city's name stays what it was: it may be the employer itself ("Santander", "Cambridge").
  - **Breaking:** a word that opens a date range is read with it, so it leaves the employer: "Software Engineer, Acme Corp, from Jan 2020 to Present" reads employer "Acme Corp", not "Acme Corp, from" (new field `rangeOpeners`: "from" in the base; "von", "de", "du", "desde" in the packs). A month and its year may be joined by a slash ("jan/2019") or by a word a pack lists (`monthYearJoiners`: Spanish and Portuguese "de", as in "marzo de 2020", LinkedIn's form).
  - **Breaking:** dates first, then the title, then the employer on a line of its own ("Sep 2018 – Aug 2021" over "Software Engineer" over "Capgemini, Toulouse") read the employer; 0.19.0 left it empty. A line that is only a date range is never joined onto the line above as its wrapped end, so a lower-case "janv. 2021 – aujourd'hui" after a bullet starts its role.
  - **Breaking:** an employer ending in a dotted abbreviation keeps its last dot: "Telefónica S.A.", "Embassy of the U.S.", "J.P.L."; "Acme Inc." still reads "Acme Inc".
  - **Breaking:** headings, degrees and titles the packs did not know. German "Weiterbildung(en)" and "Fort- und Weiterbildung" open certifications; Hindi "पेशेवर अनुभव" and "प्रोफेशनल अनुभव" open experience; LinkedIn's exported headings in each language ("Kontakt", "Top-Kenntnisse", "Principales compétences", "Contactar", "Extracto", "Contato", "Principais competências") are headings, not the name. A pack heading that extends one of the policy's ("Contactar" after "contact") is a heading. Hindi बी.एससी., बी.कॉम (6), एम.एससी., एम.कॉम (7) and पीएच.डी. (8), Québec's DEC and CEGEP (5), German "-manager(in)" and "-designer(in)" compounds and Hindi "वास्तुकार", "डिज़ाइनर", "प्रशासक" are read. A German LinkedIn export with hardly a sentence is detected as German by its CV words ("berufserfahrung", "kenntnisse", "heute", "jahre").
  - **Breaking:** an expiry word may follow its date, as Hindi writes it ("2027 तक वैध"): a new pack field, `credentialWords.expiresAfter`. French "valable jusqu'en 2027" is an expiry.
  - New language packs `es` (Spanish, Spain and Latin America) and `pt` (Portuguese, Brazil first) and region packs `ES` (Spain), `BR` (Brazil) and `PT` (Portugal, read from a +351 number), all `community` until a native speaker reviews them. Spanish is not detected by articles, "de", "san" or short prepositions, so an English resume naming "Los Angeles" or "Supermercado El Rey y Más" stays English; Spanish and Portuguese share no detection word. "Cargo en Empresa" splits where a legal form ends the company ("Diseñadora UX en Acme S.A.", Portuguese "Analista na Exemplo Ltda."), never in a title such as "Especialista en Marketing". A Spanish or Portuguese resume was read as English in 0.19.0; it is now read in its language.
  - The default policy's fingerprint is `ats-v2+7f07e3e7` in this release. The `./locales` bundle grows from 77.5 KB to 86.6 KB gzipped with the new packs, regions, cities and headings.

## 0.19.0

### Minor Changes

- 3dba46c: Choose the language a resume is read in from the CLI, and acronyms no longer make English read as another language.

  - **Breaking:** a word in capitals among lower-case words no longer counts as evidence of a language. "MIT" in "BSc, MIT, 2016" and "AB" in "Volvo AB" are acronyms, not German "mit" and "ab". An English resume with a few of them was read with the German pack attached, which changed its reading: one with "MIT", "Volvo AB", "ab test" and "Müller und Söhne GmbH" met "AB testing with Optimizely" without naming Optimizely (job match 68); it now reads as English, as it does with no pack (partial, job match 52). Two terse English resumes full of acronyms from the review probes score higher (67 → 69, 66 → 69). A line all in capitals is a heading and still counts, so German and French CVs and postings with headings in capitals ("BERUFSERFAHRUNG UND PRAKTIKA", "EXPÉRIENCE PROFESSIONNELLE", "IHRE AUFGABEN") read as before. Compared with 0.18.0 on every locale fixture, the private graded resumes and 300 generated English resumes, each alone and with five postings (2,070 runs), and on the same fixtures with their headings in capitals, every report is the same.
  - New CLI option `--lang <code>` (`de`, `fr`, `hi`, or `en` for English only) reads the resume, and a posting, in that language instead of detecting it, as the library's `languages` option does. Use it when the resume was read in the wrong language; an English resume with a German posting reads best without it. An unknown code exits with code 1 and lists the ones there are. The GitHub Action takes the same as its `language` input.
  - A test now holds every English resume to reading the same with the language packs attached as with none, so a new pack cannot change how English is read.

## 0.18.0

### Minor Changes

- cbb6a1e: Fixes for the limits 0.17.0 shipped with, and for a few cases where it still read a resume worse than 0.16.0.

  - **Breaking:** a leave or career break dated like a job is no longer read as a role, in text, in JSON Resume and ats-resume documents (also a JSON Resume entry named "Career Break" with no position), and in an AI repair. "Parental leave, 03/2024 – Present", "Career break 2019 – 2020", "Sabbatical", German "Elternzeit ab 03/2024", "Mutterschutz", "Auszeit" and French "Congé parental", "Année sabbatique" add no months of experience and no title for the seniority check. A German CV with 48 months of work and "Elternzeit ab 03/2024" read 80 months; it reads 48. A role that only mentions a leave ("Visiting Professor (sabbatical)", "HR Manager, Parental Leave Programs") is still a role, and so is a leave whose bracket or employer names a job title or an organisation: "Sabbatical (Visiting Researcher, Stanford)", "Sabbatical, Stanford University", "Elternzeit (Teilzeit als Entwickler bei Beispiel AG)". The words are a new policy list, `resumeParse.leaveWords`, which the German and French packs extend; the default policy's fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** a dated line that opens with a capitalised past-tense action verb, holds no job-title word before its dates and only lowercase words and numbers between the verb and them, is no longer read as a role when words or a full stop follow its dates, or when it ends in an everyday open end ("continuing", "onwards") after words of its own. "Analysed 2017 thru 2018 data", "Mentored two junior engineers since 2012.", "Maintained a legacy system originally built 2008 - 2011 by another team." and "Mentored 5 interns 2017 – continuing" each added a phantom role, and most added months of experience (36 → 129 months on one test resume). Headers that start like verbs ("Lead Engineer", "Managed Services Engineer", "Integrated Device Technology"), a line its dates end ("Founded startup 2017 – 2019", "Owned and operated a bakery 2015 – 2019", "Founded startup 2017 – Present", "Hired 2017 – 2019" under a title) and "Senior Engineer 2017 – continuing" are still roles. Other dated sentences are still read as roles, as in 0.17.0: one that opens otherwise ("Grew revenue every quarter from 2017 onward.", "Responsible for a codebase written in 2005 through 2009 and still in use."), one with a capitalised word before its dates ("Mentored two junior Java engineers since 2012."), and any line in a script without case, such as Hindi.
  - **Breaking:** a tagline before a title is no longer read as the name, even when the email or a profile link spells it. "Open Source | Software Engineer" with github.com/open-source gave the name "Open Source"; it gives none, and a name on the next line is still read. The same holds for "Machine Learning", "Data Science", "Full Stack" and "Cloud Native", and for the "Surname, Given" form. The taglines are a new policy list, `resumeParse.notNames`, read only to find the name; job matching is unchanged. A name holding a skill's word ("Sean Go", "Go Min-jun", "Vue Nguyen", "Spark Lee", "Rust Cohle") is still read.
  - **Breaking:** a "Languages" list of programming languages is not a list of spoken languages, wherever it is: under a "Languages" heading, on a "Languages:" line, or as a JSON Resume or ats-resume `languages` list. An item counts as a programming language when the policy knows it as a skill ("Python", "Go", "SQL", "TypeScript") or it holds a programming symbol ("C++", "C#", "Node.js"). Such a list no longer stops an English resume from meeting "Fluent English" at C1 from the language it is written in ("Languages" with "Python, Go" read unverifiable, and a JSON Resume with `languages: [Python, Go]` read missing; both are met), and gives no spoken-language rows. A list naming any spoken language ("English (B1), Python") still decides, and an item the policy does not know is a spoken language, as in 0.17.0: "ASL", "isiZulu", "IRISH", but also "HTML" or "GraphQL". This corrects the 0.17.0 note that such a list gives no credit.
  - AI repair fills a phone number written with an extension word or a hash again, as 0.16.0 did ("+1 202 555 0143 extension 12", "+1 415 555 0134 #12"), and a toll-free vanity number ("1-800-FLOWERS", "1-800-GOT-JUNK"). A full toll-free number keeps its extension apart ("1-800-555-0199 EXT 12"); letters after any other number, or after a full one, still keep it out: "(555) 010-2020 CELL", "1-800-555-0199 CELL", "2019-2021 AB".
  - Requirement rows count years per skill from the lines read as roles, so a dropped leave or sentence line does not shift them.

## 0.17.0

### Minor Changes

- 85578af: Smaller fixes from the same audit.

  - **Breaking:** "or related field" in a degree requirement no longer lets work experience stand in for the degree. A Bachelor's with 9 years is now missing against "Master's degree in Computer Science or related field", not partial ("…or equivalent experience"), and the ask gives the same result with or without "a". "Bachelor's in CS or a related field with 4+ years" needs the degree and 4 years of any work: 10 years and no degree is missing, and a B.S. Computer Science with 11 years is met. A field the ask abbreviates is held by the words the policy says it stands for (a new `keywordMatch.requirements.fieldAbbreviations`: CS, EE, AI, ML, HR, BA), read in the degree's own words: never by initials ("B.S. Chemistry, Stanford University" is not CS) or a school's name ("Colorado State", "Art Institute of Chicago"). A degree in a field the ask does not name is partial. The default policy moves that pattern from `keywordMatch.requirements.equivalence` to a new `keywordMatch.requirements.relatedField`, and adds `keywordMatch.requirements.fieldAbbreviations`; its fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** the German pack reads "-kenntnisse" compounds as languages, with their level. "Englischkenntnisse (C1)" and "sehr gute Französischkenntnisse" in a resume are language rows at their level. "Gute Französischkenntnisse" and "mit guten Englischkenntnissen" in a posting are language requirements at B1, not missing skills: a row of "Englisch (A1)" is missing it and "Englisch – Grundkenntnisse" is partial. "Basiskenntnisse" reads as A2 and "Muttersprachniveau" as C2. A language named twice in one ask is asked once, and is reported by its name ("Englisch"), not the compound.
  - **Breaking:** a language requirement is met at C1 by the language the resume's own sentences (its bullets and summary) are written in, when the resume lists no languages, no line names that language, and at least three of its sentence lines (bullets, a summary) are written in it, most of them holding the language's own words, so one English summary over Spanish, Portuguese, Italian or Dutch bullets does not make an English resume. A "Languages" heading counts as a list of languages even when it lists programming languages ("Languages: Python, Go"), so it gives no credit. An English resume without a languages list now meets "Fluent English", and a German one "Fließend Deutsch"; both were unverifiable. It is never read as native: "Native English speaker" is partial. Headings and dates never count, so a Spanish resume with English headings, or a Portuguese JSON Resume, does not meet "Fluent English". A stated level such as "English: basic" or "English (A2)" still decides, and a language a host passes in `languages` is not credited unless the sentences show it.
  - **Breaking:** policy weights are capped at 1,000: rule and band `weight`, and `keywordMatch.requiredWeight`, `preferredWeight`, `responsibilitiesWeight` and `defaultWeight`. Two weights of 1e308 summed to Infinity, so the score read 100 while a category read 0. A larger value, Infinity included, now throws `AtsPolicyError` with the field's path, and `policy.schema.json` carries the cap.
  - **Breaking:** a name followed by a job title on the first line is read when one email or one profile link spells every word of it: "Mira Kestrel | Senior Software Engineer", "MIRA KESTREL · Data Analyst" or "Mira Kestrel, Senior Software Engineer" with mira.kestrel@…, mkestrel@… or linkedin.com/in/mira-kestrel. These gave no name. One word is not enough (mira@… alone, or "San Francisco | Software Engineer" with francisco.lopez@…), and a link's address words ("in", "linkedin", "github") never count, so a tagline, a city or an employer is not taken for the name. "Kestrel, Mira" is read as "Mira Kestrel", and "KESTREL, MIRA" as "MIRA KESTREL", under the same condition; otherwise it is no name, so "Java, Spring" or "Munich, Bavaria" names no one, and a state code is never a given name ("Austin, TX"). Either reading gives way to a name on a later line ("Jane Doe" under "Austin, TX" or "Morgan Stanley | Associate" is the name). An employer before the title ("Acme Corp | Senior Engineer") is never the name.
  - **Breaking:** an education line split by tab stops or column gaps gives its school: "B.S. Computer Science⇥University of Oregon⇥2018" gives "University of Oregon", not "B.S. Computer Science University of Oregon". A gap after a short joining word, in any case, stays inside the name: "University of", "University Of" or "UNIVERSITY OF", two spaces, then "California, Berkeley" gives "University of California", while "University of Iowa⇥B.S. …" or "BS⇥Stanford University" still splits. In capitals, a short last word before the gap still joins what follows ("UNIVERSITY OF IOWA⇥B.S."), as before. A date range in brackets, spaced or not ("( 2014 - 2018 )"), no longer leaves "( )" or "(" in the school's name.
  - **Breaking:** JSON Resume drops empty entries before cutting a list to its 200-entry limit; 200 empty roles in front hid every real one. A file without `basics` (when a role has `position` or a school `institution`), with `basics` that is not an object, or with `work` (or any list) given as one object is read as structure; it was read as plain text, with 0 roles. A `basics` that is only a string is the name when it passes the checks a printed name gets (`"basics": "Richard Hendriks"`, or `"王小明"`); a job title or a heading (`"Senior Software Engineer"`) is not.
  - **Breaking:** a job posting is read to its first 20,000 characters on every path. `normalizeJobText`, `jobHtmlToText` and `jobTextFromHtml` cut at 12,000 by default, so a posting from the CLI's `--job` or `--job-url`, the MCP server, or a host using them lost everything past 12,000 while `check` reads 20,000. A 12,681-character posting with its requirements last scored a job match of 36 with no requirements; it now scores 4, with three judged missing. `MAX_JOB_TEXT_CHARS` is 20,000. The helpers cut only when given `maxChars`: pass it if you store or send their output. A longer posting is cut in `check`, and `parsingWarnings` says so.
  - A rate limit, server fault, timeout or network error is retried after 1 s, then 2, 4, 8 and 16 s, or after the provider's `retry-after` (decimal seconds or an HTTP date; "0x10", "1e3" or a blank value is ignored, not read as 16 s, 1,000 s or no wait); `retries: 5` made six calls 0 to 1 ms apart. A `retry-after` over a minute is not retried. A call's `signal` ends a wait. `onRetry` receives `delayMs`, and `LlmProviderError` has `retryAfterMs`.
  - `timeoutMs` holds when a `fetch` you pass in ignores the abort signal; such a call never returned.
  - An error sent with HTTP 200 and no answer (OpenAI-compatible `{"error":…}`, Anthropic `{"type":"error",…}`, Gemini `[{"error":…}]`) is a `provider` error with its message; it read as `invalid_output: Empty response.` and was retried. An answer that comes with an empty `error` (`{}` or `null`), as some gateways add, is still the answer. An error given as a bare string is not retried when it names an invalid key, auth, a permission or something not found ("Invalid API key"), as with an error `type`. Error messages also quote a string `detail` (FastAPI, vLLM), Gemini's error list, and a `message` beside an empty `error.message`, under the same length, line and key-redaction rules.
  - On Linux and macOS a path that starts with `//` is read; it was refused as a network share. Windows still refuses shares.
  - **Breaking:** hidden text drawn outside its clip is found. A PDF that clips text to an empty or far-away rectangle (`0 0 0 0 re W n`), or places it outside a form's box, had it read as visible: readiness 27 on the audit's sample, now 0. A PDF annotation (a note added with Preview's text tool) is measured as it is drawn: in its own rectangle, with none of the clip, colour or transparency the page set, so a note on a page that clips to its text area is not hidden text. Page text that an annotation's white box covers is. A highlight stays visible: a yellow box multiplied over a line, or one at 40% opacity, is not flagged, nor a highlight pdf.js draws itself, which 0.16.0 flagged. A shape drawn after text in Multiply, Screen, Darken, Lighten, Difference or Exclusion hides it only when, blended, the text is lost against the page: a white Screen box over black text is flagged, a yellow Multiply box is not (0.16.0 flagged a Multiply box drawn after text). A shape in any other blend mode covers as a normal fill does, as in 0.16.0.
  - **Breaking:** text whose blend mode leaves the background unchanged is hidden text: black text with Screen or Lighten on the white page, white text with Multiply or Darken on a dark band. Multiply of dark text on a light band, and other honest uses, are unchanged.
  - **Breaking:** an image of one colour no longer excuses the text on it. Invisible (`3 Tr`) text over a blank white image is no longer taken for a scan's OCR layer, and white text on a white image (or black on black) is judged against the image's colour. A scanned page with its OCR text over a picture of the words is still not flagged.
  - **Breaking:** an image with a soft mask a shade short of opaque (a pixel at 254 of 255) covers the text under it, as an opaque shape does; a mask lets text show only below 90% opacity.

- 114ec96: Fixes from an audit of the engine.

  - **Breaking:** text in a square-cornered bordered box or a tinted band of a PDF is no longer read as hidden text. A border filled as one frame, its outer rectangle with the inner cut out (`re re f*`), was taken for a solid box of its colour, and a translucent fill (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06)`) for its full colour, so dark text in either failed the hidden-text check. A Chrome-printed resume with one tinted section scored 56 instead of 86; one with a table whose cells are framed so, 38 instead of 68. The inside of a border is now what lies under it, unless the border lies under most of the text: a small hole under the middle of a line does not make it visible. A translucent fill is blended with what lies under it; a fill that lets less than a tenth of what lies under it show counts as opaque, so a 99% white box over a picture, or four 50% layers, still hides white text. Translucent boxes of the text's own colour that together cover 70% or more of what lies beneath still hide it (black text on an 85% black box, or on three 50% ones); white text on an 85% navy band, black text on a 50% grey band and a chip tinted with its text's colour stay clean.
    - Still hidden: white text inside a border or on a faint tint, which was missed before.
    - A page splits at most 2,000 boxes from its filled shapes; past that, a shape is read as solid. A file drawing hundreds of intricate frames could otherwise stop the hidden-text check altogether.
    - Not changed: a rounded border (Chrome draws `border-radius` with curves) is still read as a solid box, so dark text in a dark rounded chip is still flagged.
  - A PDF page the file declares millions of points wide is read in the time of any other page. The column search stepped across the declared width: a 50,000,000-point page took 12 seconds, so a small file of such pages held the reader for minutes. It now searches at most 14,400 points, the widest page a PDF allows.
  - A document with many copies of one link is read in the time of any other. Each link's address was looked for in the whole text, once per copy: 2,000 copies over 2 MB of text took a second, and a small Word file of repeated links took minutes. Each address is now looked for once, among the text's words holding ".", "@" or "/", and the searches stop after 50,000,000 characters (a thousand searches of a full resume).
  - An HTML page a Word document embeds (`w:altChunk`) is read once, however often the document names it, and the embedded pages share 8 MB between them. Each name read the page again, up to 8 MB each: one 2 MB page named 30 times took 1.6 seconds. A page past what is left is not read.
  - **Breaking:** more ways of writing a current role's dates are read, so the role is no longer dropped, and the experience and seniority read from it no longer halve. A role dated "Jun 2021 - Till now" was missing from the work history, with no warning.
    - English: "Till now", "Continuing", "Jun 2021 onwards" (and "onward"), and "thru" between two dates.
    - A month with its zero and a two-digit year, between two such dates or before an open end: "06/21 - Present", "01/15 - 05/21". Alone, "10/10" is still no date, and "7/10 - 9/10" is a score. A span of two such dates must end the line or a column: "Rated 08/10 - 10/10 by users" is no role.
    - German: "– bis heute", "bis jetzt", "bis dato", and "ab 03/2020". Hindi: "अभी तक", and "मार्च 2020 से" with nothing after "से". French: "hiver" as a season (January to March).
    - "Continuing", "onwards" ("onward"), German "ab" and Hindi "से" are everyday words too: they date a role only where their date ends the line or a column. "Jun 2021 onwards" and "ab 03/2020" are current roles; "2020 onwards, growth of 30%" and "Jan 2017 continuing support for 3 apps" in a bullet are no role. "AB" in capitals is a company's suffix: "Volvo AB 2018 – 2021" is a role that ended in 2021. A since date still to come dates no role: "verfügbar ab 01/2027" is no current role. Any other open end may have a place after it: "Jun 2021 Present remote" and "03/2020 heute bei Siemens" are current roles.
    - **Breaking:** the default policy's `resumeParse.openEnded` gains "till now", "continuing", "onwards", "onward", "current role" and "current position", and `resumeParse.rangeWords` gains "thru". A new `resumeParse.lineEndDateWords` ("continuing", "onwards", "onward"; the German pack adds "ab", the Hindi pack "से") lists the open ends and since words that date a role only where their date ends the line. The default policy's fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** every kind of line break starts a new line: a lone carriage return (old Mac files, some Word exports), a vertical tab, a form feed, NEL, and the Unicode line and paragraph separators. Before, such a resume read as one line: an invented one scored 85 instead of 91, with its name and one of its two roles lost.
  - **Breaking:** text in a PDF font that uses one of the standard CJK character maps (`UniJIS-UCS2-H`, `UniGB-UCS2-H` and the like, common in Chinese, Japanese and Korean resumes) is read. pdf.js was never told where its character maps are, so that text came out empty. Both PDF passes now get them, and the table pass no longer evaluates code from the file either (`isEvalSupported: false`, as the text pass already had).
  - **Breaking:** AI answers are held to their fields' shapes. `mergeGrounded` fills a contact field only with that kind of value: an email address, its domain in any script (`jane@bücher.de`); a phone number's characters and 7 to 15 digits, read with its digits and dashes folded (Arabic-Indic or fullwidth digits, the non-breaking hyphen Word writes, an extension after a comma), and not a date range alone, years alone ("2019 2020 2021"), an IP address or an ISBN; a name of up to twelve capitalised words (pronouns in brackets and "3rd" aside), not a heading ("EXPERIENCE"), a sentence, one of the resume's own job titles or employers, or a phrase led by a job-title or organisation word ("Senior Engineer, Acme Corporation"); surnames such as Head, Bank or Cook are kept. A phone's label and note ("Mobile:", "(US)") are dropped before its shape is checked, and the number is stored without them. Any words of the resume used to pass, so a model, or text planted in the resume, could fill the email field with "Acme Corporation". `convertResume` compares a link whole, scheme and all: "https://fabrikam.ltd" no longer passes as the words "Fabrikam Ltd". A link the resume writes in brackets or guillemets ("[janedoe.dev]"), or with such marks in its path ("janedoe.dev/[draft]"), still counts.
  - A provider's HTTP error no longer quotes its body in `AtsAiError`'s message: a gateway that echoes the request put the resume's name, email and phone there, and so into a host's logs. The message quotes only the provider's own error text (a JSON body's `error.message`, or a one-line text body, up to 200 characters, keys redacted), as in "Provider returned HTTP 400: Invalid value for 'temperature'.", else just "Provider returned HTTP 400.". Text broken by any line break, a lone carriage return or U+2028 included, is not quoted.
  - **Breaking:** the right to work is compared by country. A statement naming only other countries than the posting asks about is no longer evidence: "Authorized to work in the US" or a green card no longer meets "right to work in the UK", and the row is unverifiable instead of met. A statement naming no country is read as before. "Must be a British citizen" is read as a citizenship ask, not as a skill. A heading or label alone ("Work Authorization") is no statement.
    - A citizenship meets a citizenship ask only for its own country, and each clause of a line is read for its own country: "Indian citizen; authorized to work in the US" shows a right to work in the US, not U.S. citizenship. "Latin American citizen" is no American citizenship. A bare "US" is read as the US beside "and", "&" or "/" ("Canada/US") and before a right-to-work word ("US Permanent Resident").
    - A list of countries is read past commas and brackets ("Authorized to work in the US, Canada and the UK", "Canada (PR) and the U.S. (TN visa)"), and a place the policy's countries do not name ("Ontario") leaves the line read as before. A nationality states that citizenship: "Citizenship: Indian", "British national", "EU passport", "Citizen of an EU member state", "Dual US-UK citizen".
    - Ireland is a country of its own: an Irish citizen may work in the UK and the EU, and a British or EU citizen in Ireland, but "Irish citizen" meets no U.S. or British citizenship ask.
    - **Breaking:** the default policy has a new `keywordMatch.requirements.countries`, each a `name`, its `patterns`, and optionally `citizensWorkIn` (other countries, by name, whose right to work its citizens hold): US (with "green card"; "us" only as "the US", "in the US" or "US citizen", never the pronoun), UK (with "Northern Ireland"), EU (with its member states), Ireland, Canada, Australia and India; US also reads "America" and "the States". A new `requirements.placeJoiners` lists the words that join places in a list. `requirements.authorization` and `requirements.citizenship` gain British, UK, EU, American, Canadian, Australian, Irish and Indian citizenship, and nationalities ("Indian national", "British passport holder"). The default policy's fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** a learner's language level no longer meets a fluent one. "Currently learning", "still learning" (A1), "school level" (A2) and German "Schulkenntnisse" (A2) are read, so "Spanish (currently learning)" no longer meets "Fluent Spanish", nor "Französisch (Schulkenntnisse)" "verhandlungssicheres Französisch". A level no word reads ("excellent") is still met, as a row with no level is. The default policy's `resumeParse.languageLevels` gains those three, and its fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** a negation about something else beside a clearance no longer cancels it. "Active TS/SCI clearance, no lapses since 2015" read as no clearance; it now meets "TS/SCI clearance required". "Active Secret clearance; Relocation: No" and "Active Top Secret clearance; not active duty military" meet it too. A negation counts in the clearance's own clause ("No active Secret clearance"), a "no" alone in the clause right after it ("TS/SCI clearance (no)", "Secret clearance: no"), and a negated phrase anywhere in its own sentence up to a semicolon: "Secret clearance (not active)", "TS/SCI clearance (not granted)", "…, not yet granted", "not in use since 2018", "Held TS/SCI clearance, not renewed". The default policy has a new `requirements.notHeldNearby` with those phrases ("not active", "not current", "not valid", "not held", "not obtained", "not renewed", "not cleared", "not (yet) granted", "issued", "approved", "in use", "no longer"); its fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** an expired, future-dated or in-progress certification no longer meets a requirement naming it, whatever words the requirement uses. "CISSP (expired 2021)" met "Active CISSP", "CISSP required" and "Must hold a current CISSP", and "CISSP (in progress, expected Dec 2026)" met "CISSP certification required". Such a requirement is now partial, with the row as the evidence and a detail saying why ("CISSP: expired 2021", "CISSP: not yet held"), unless a held row or the work history shows the skill. A row with no expiry is held, and an expiry needs an expiry word ("expired 2021", "valid until 2027"): a certificate dated by a plain range ("Google Data Analytics Certificate, Coursera, 2021 – 2022") is held. An expired certification named like a skill ("Kubernetes, expired 2022") does not hide that skill in the work history or skills list. In a one-line list, an in-progress word marks only its own item: "Six Sigma Green Belt (in progress), PMP, 2019" holds PMP, and "working towards AZ-104" or "renewal in progress" marks nothing unfinished. A certification listed twice, a lapsed row and its renewal, keeps its latest row, and "expired 2021, renewed 2023" is held. An in-progress word in a label ("Pursuing excellence: CISSP") does not mark the row unfinished; at the label's end ("Currently pursuing: CISSP") it does. The default policy has a new `requirements.inProgress`: "in progress", "pursuing", "studying for", "working towards"; `resumeParse.credentialWords.issued` gains "renewed" and "recertified".
  - **Breaking:** a verb no longer meets the skill its stem spells. "Reacted to 40 outages" met React, "Sparked a redesign" Spark, "rusted runbooks" Rust, and "R&D" met R. A word folded onto a skill the policy spells as its own stem, by an ending other than a plural, stays itself ("APIs" still meets API, "Tested" still meets Testing). Two skills joined by "&" are each read ("C&C++" meets C, "AI&ML" meets AI and ML), and two single letters joined by "&" are one abbreviation: "P&L", "M&A" and "R&D" meet the same abbreviation, and "R&D" does not meet R. The default policy's `keywordMatch.phrases` gains "spark" and "rust", so they are named skills; its fingerprint changes.
  - **Breaking:** the invisible-characters check no longer counts bidirectional embeddings (U+202A to U+202C), which Word writes around the words of a right-to-left document: an honest Hebrew or Arabic resume lost 10 points. They set a run's direction and reverse no letters. Overrides (U+202D, U+202E) and isolates around words are still counted.
  - `analyze` no longer turns a reply that says nothing into an empty success. A reply wrapped in another key (`{"analysis": {…}}`), bare, in a fence or with prose around it, or with every field empty or blank (or only keyword suggestions when no posting was given), parsed as an empty analysis, with no error and no retry: a paid call, nothing back. It is now `invalid_output`, which is retried. A reply that shows a JSON example before its answer is read for the answer: each object in the reply is tried until one fits, and an object is read whole, never for something inside it. A 4.8 MB nested reply after prose is read in about half a second. A sparse answer (only keyword suggestions for a posting, say) is still one.
  - A reply cut off at `maxTokens` whose answer is itself cut off, or cut off inside its reasoning, is `truncated`. One holding a complete inner object was read for that object, or retried up to 3 times as `invalid_output`, paying for the same cut-off reply each time. A reply cut off after its complete answer (a closed fenced block, or a whole object followed by prose) is still read.
  - **Breaking:** a JSON Resume or `ats-resume` role whose end is an open end in words other than English "Present" is current. "heute", "aujourd'hui", "Current role" or "Till now" gave a role with no end and one month of experience (8 years read as 1 month, and "5+ years" as partial); an end that is an open end as a whole, in any language the policy and its packs read ("heute", "Current role", "- Present."), is now read as one. An end with more after the open end ("Present 2021", "Current role ended 2020", "Heute nicht"), one it cannot read ("soon", "Not current"), or Hindi "से" alone is still no end. Education entries read the same way.
  - A huge paste is read without reading all of it: resume text is normalised 100,000 characters at a time until the 50,000 it keeps are filled, reading at most 2,000,000. A 40 MB paste with numbers took one to two seconds and its size in memory again; it now takes milliseconds. Invisible characters are counted on what was read and do not use up the 50,000.

## 0.16.0

### Minor Changes

- d88dc12: The requirements table judges the seniority a posting's title asks for.

  - **Breaking:** a posting whose first line is a title naming a level ("Senior Backend Engineer", "Staff Software Engineer", "Junior Developer") gets a new first row with `kind: "seniority"`. The resume's latest title and its years judge it:
    - **met** by a latest title at or above the level with at least half the years the level takes, or by those years alone when the title names no level;
    - **partial** with the title alone (under half the years), or with a lower title and the years;
    - **missing** otherwise.
    - `detail` says what was compared: "Latest title senior, 10 years in the work history; staff asked (8+ years)". Of several current roles, the highest level counts. An entry level takes no years, so a resume without dated roles meets it.
  - A posting gets no row, and its table is unchanged, when its first line names no level, ends as a sentence ends (".", "!", "?"), is longer than eight words, or names no job besides its level word: an employer's name such as "Principal Health Partners" or "Lead Bank". A level that ends the title ("Team Lead, Customer Support") or an entry level ("Data Science Intern") is a job itself. A French level after its noun is read ("Chargé de clientèle junior", "Ingénieur logiciel expérimenté"). A level named in a requirement ("work with senior stakeholders") is not read. No score changes: the job match does not read the table.
  - **Breaking:** the policy has a new `keywordMatch.requirements.seniorityLevels`, lowest first, each a `name`, the `years` it takes and title `patterns`. The default ladder: entry (intern, trainee, apprentice, graduate, junior; 0 years), mid (mid-level, intermediate; 2), senior (senior, sr; 5), lead (lead, principal, and staff before an engineering or science noun; 8). "Staff Accountant", "Staff Nurse", "Senior Living" and "Lead Generation" name no level, and manager and director titles are a ladder of their own. The default policy's fingerprint changes.
  - A language pack adds title words to a level by name (`requirements.seniorityLevels`): German adds Praktikant, Werkstudent, Auszubildende and Berufseinsteiger (entry); French adds stagiaire, alternant and débutant (entry), and confirmé and expérimenté (senior). The French pack also reads "chargé(e) de clientèle, de mission, d'affaires…" as a job title, in postings and on resumes.

- 85765ab: A bullet copied word for word into a few roles is no longer read as keyword stuffing.

  - **Breaking:** the readiness score rises by the keyword-stuffing deduction (10 points with the default policy) for a resume whose one sentence, such as "Mentored three junior colleagues into their first promotion", appears once under each of three or four roles. The check read it as a line pasted again and again. A sentence is one with a stopword or that opens with an action verb, so a terse bullet ("Mentored junior engineers through weekly pairing sessions") counts too. Of 3,000 generated resumes, 46 (1.5%) carried such a bullet and failed the check; they now pass, and no other result moves.
    - Still stuffing: the same sentence in five roles or more; a sentence pasted three times under one role, or outside the roles; a run of terms ("python kubernetes docker aws") or a list ("python, kubernetes, docker and kafka") repeated anywhere, in lower case too.

### Patch Changes

- 9cff50a: `policy.schema.json` is strict: an editor now flags a misspelt key in a policy file, such as `rulez` at the top or `wieght` in a rule, which `parseAtsPolicy` drops without a word. Every object with a fixed set of keys allows no other key. Maps keep any key: `synonyms`, `implies`, `numberWords`, advice `targets`, month and season names, language levels and names, and a region's `rules`. `$schema` stays allowed at the top. `parseAtsPolicy` is unchanged: it still drops unknown keys.
- d939b84: `readJobFile`, and so the CLI's `--job` and the MCP server's job path, reads a posting saved as `.xhtml` as a web page, as `readResumeFile` reads a resume. It was refused as an unsupported type.

## 0.15.0

### Minor Changes

- b20dd84: Keyword stuffing is caught when a line names a few skills again and again, each under five times.

  - **Breaking:** the readiness score drops for a resume with such a line. "Keywords: Python Kubernetes AWS Docker Go Kafka", written four times on one line, passed the keyword-stuffing check, because each term made up only 16% of the line. The check now also counts the terms of a line together: terms named three times or more each, totalling 10 words or more and half the line, are stuffing. That resume now fails the check: with the default policy, a sales manager's resume with the line added falls from 92 to 82, where it had scored the same as without it.
    - A list split by commas, pipes or semicolons is judged as before, and so is a skills line that names each term once. No other resume among the 3,945 in the tests and the benchmark changes its result.
    - The job match is unchanged: the terms are on the page, and naming them once gives the same match.

## 0.14.0

### Minor Changes

- ca0e088: The deprecated API and the old policy shapes are removed.

  - **Breaking:** `AtsScoringService` is gone. Call `check(resume, policy?, options?)`, which gives the same report.
  - **Breaking:** `level` on `AtsParsedEducation`, `highestDegree` on `AtsParsedResume`, `AtsDegreeLevel` and `DEGREE_LABELS` are gone. Read `isced`, `highestIsced` and `ISCED_LABELS`.
  - **Breaking:** a policy's `resumeParse.degrees` is keyed by ISCED level (`"2"` to `"8"`) only. The old `diploma`/`associate`/`bachelor`/`master`/`doctorate` keys are refused.
  - **Breaking:** a `position` rule no longer takes `emailPattern` or `phonePattern`. It locates the email address and phone number the parser recovered, as the default policy always has.
  - **Breaking:** `AtsLayoutSignals.hiddenTextSample` is gone. `hiddenText` holds all of the hidden text, and the hidden-text rule quotes its first 80 characters.
  - A DOCX is unzipped once per read, where it was unzipped up to six times.
  - Bundle sizes (gzipped): `.` from 102.9 to 102.6 KB.

## 0.13.0

### Minor Changes

- 97b2671: Hidden text is set aside by what a reader puts in the text, white text inside a visible line is cut from it, and the bundle sizes ship in the package.

  - **Breaking:** the job match, the requirements and the missing keywords change for a resume with hidden text.
    - **The layout says which of the hidden text the text holds**, as the new `AtsLayoutSignals.hiddenTextRead`: on a PDF all of it; in a Word document all but the runs a header or footer marks hidden, which its text leaves out; in an HTML resume none, as hidden elements are left out of the text. Only that text is set aside, so a visible line that repeats hidden text no reader keeps (a Word header's hidden run, a page's `display: none` block) is no longer set aside. A layout without the field (an older extractor, or a host that passes only `hiddenText`) is read as 0.12.0 reads it.
    - **White text drawn after visible text on one line is cut from that line**, word by word, and the rest of the line stays: a white "Kafka Kubernetes" after "Senior Engineer" no longer counts. A word is cut only when every copy of it left in the kept lines, inside other words and in any case too ("Kafka-based", "kafka"), is one the hidden text owes, and a stretch under four characters, one two lines hold, or one the hidden text spells out as another copy of a line set aside (a white footer on every page, one Word header in two parts) is not cut.
    - **Hidden text read in another order than the lines** (a second column's hidden runs first) is set aside line by line when it splits into the lines' texts one way only.
    - No phrase is read across a line set aside or a cut, nor across a kept copy of a line whose other copies are set aside, and a requirement's evidence quotes the text without a mark where a cut was.
    - On 6,000 generated resumes against 0.12.0, no resume is read worse: hidden-only skills matched fell from 902 to 14, and visible skills lost to hidden text from 1,267 to 43. The 14 are white text after visible text that repeats a separate hidden line word for word, which the text alone cannot tell from a line listed twice and read once; it is left, so no visible skill is cut, and the hidden-text rule still fails and caps the job match. A test now holds these figures on 600 seeded resumes, so a later change cannot raise them unnoticed.
  - **A job posting or a JSON file is decoded as a resume's text is.** A UTF-16 posting (Notepad's "Unicode", PowerShell 5's `>`) was read as UTF-8: it matched nothing and listed its letters as missing keywords. A Windows-1252 posting lost its accented letters ("D�veloppeur"), and a `--policy` or JSON resume file saved with a byte-order mark was refused as "not valid JSON". `readJobFile` and `parseJsonFile` now read them all.
  - **A job posting with no readable text is refused** with `AtsFileError` ("has no readable job posting text"), where `readJobFile` returned an empty posting: `ats-engine check --job` and the Action scored no job match and said nothing. The MCP server refused it already.
  - **A Word file whose relationships part nests past eight levels is refused as unreadable.** Each level was read with every namespace prefix above it: a 26 KB file took 8 seconds to read and a 52 KB one ran out of memory. Real files nest two levels.
  - **AI:** `analyze` redacts the resume's email addresses in one pass, where it ran the text once per distinct address: thousands of them took seconds of CPU. A model's reply is searched for a fenced JSON block without a pattern that scanned to the end of the reply from every fence left open.
  - **The Action refuses a `min-score` the CLI refuses**: "0x32" and "1e1" were read as 50 and 10.
  - **The bundle sizes ship in the package**, as `@veriworkly/ats-engine/sizes.json`: each subpath's size, minified and gzipped, as `npm run size` measured it for this release, with its budget. The budgets are raised ahead of need: `.` to 106 KB, `/locales` to 79.5 (room for one more language pack), `/ai` to 75, `/node` to 22.5, `withLocales` alone to 50.5.
  - Bundle sizes (gzipped): `.` from 101.8 to 102.9 KB.

## 0.12.0

### Minor Changes

- 0e3eebc: Fixes from an audit of 0.10.0.

  - **Breaking:** a visible line is no longer set aside as hidden because the hidden text repeats it. When lines, in reading order, joined are the hidden text whole, and it splits into the lines' texts one way only, exactly those lines are set aside, the later copy of a line written twice. Otherwise (a split two ways, a second column's hidden runs read first, or the hidden text cut at 5,000 characters) each stretch of hidden text sets aside one line, the longest claiming theirs first, and a visible line across two hidden ones never frees them. A line under four characters is never set aside, as before, and the lines either side of one set aside are not read as one phrase. So a resume with a visible "Kubernetes" skill and a hidden "Kubernetes Terraform Kafka" block keeps its Kubernetes in the job match (it fell from 100 to 0 and was reported missing), and a visible "Docker Kubernetes" across the wrap of a hidden "Python Java Docker / Kubernetes Terraform" block keeps both. Hidden text is left out as before: on 7,000 generated resumes no hidden word or phrase is matched that 0.11.0 did not match, and visible skills lost to hidden text fell from 4,162 to 16 on 3,000 of them. A hidden run at the end of a visible line is still read with that line, as before; the hidden-text rule fails and caps the job match. The job match, the requirements and the missing keywords change for such resumes.
  - **Breaking:** the `languages` option is read in any case, and an id no attached pack has throws `AtsPolicyError` naming the attached ones. `languages: ["DE"]` or `["deu"]` was dropped without a word, so a German resume lost its roles and was judged by English writing rules. `[]`, or the policy's own language (`"en"`), still reads with the base only.
  - **AI:** a provider's answer, an error's included, is read to 4 MB and refused past it before it is parsed; a declared larger `content-length` is refused unread. An error past it keeps its status, and stays retryable when its status is (a gateway's error page is not the model's answer). A `fetch` you pass in whose body is not a web stream (node-fetch's, a test double's) is read whole with `text()`, then measured. The timeout bounded how long a call took, not how much it received.
  - **`/node`:** `readResumeFile` and `readJobFile` take an `extract` option, the function that reads a PDF's or DOCX's bytes, so a host can run `/node/child` while keeping the path, type and size checks.
  - **Action:** each run writes its report to its own file in `RUNNER_TEMP`, so a job checking two resumes keeps both reports. Read its path from the `report` output; a step that opened `$RUNNER_TEMP/ats-report.json` by name must use the output instead.
  - Docs: a report repeats for the same input, policy and reference date (`now`), as tenure and "present" are counted from it.
  - Bundle sizes (gzipped): `.` from 100.9 to 101.8 KB, `/locales` from 75.5 to 75.6, and the AI adapters from 1.9 to 2.2 KB each.

## 0.11.0

### Minor Changes

- 13ffd6d: **The JSON Schema of a scoring policy ships in the package**, as `@veriworkly/ats-engine/policy.schema.json` (JSON Schema draft 2020-12, generated at build from the schema `parseAtsPolicy` validates with). Point a policy file's `$schema` at it, or at `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@veriworkly/ats-engine@<version>/dist/policy.schema.json`, for completion and checking in an editor. Before, only the language and region packs had a schema (`atsLanguagePackJsonSchema`, `atsRegionPackJsonSchema`), and writing a whole policy meant reading the source. `parseAtsPolicy` stays the authority: it also compiles the patterns and refuses two rules with one id, which a schema cannot say. The schema is a file, not a module, so no bundle grows. The package's homepage is now the documentation, [docs.veriworkly.com/ats-engine](https://docs.veriworkly.com/ats-engine), and the README and `llms.txt` link to it. Scores, recovered fields and the report are the same for every input.

## 0.10.0

### Minor Changes

- 97d2967: **`ats-engine check --job-url <url>` reads a job posting on Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby** from the board's public JSON API, so a posting no longer has to be saved first: `ats-engine check resume.pdf --job-url https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/123`. It reads the posting's title and description, and the employer's name, left out of the keywords as it is for a saved `.html` page: Greenhouse's, or, as Lever's and Ashby's APIs name none, the board's name in the link. A Greenhouse posting is read from its board page, its `?gh_jid=` link or the embed a careers page frames (`/embed/job_app?for=…&token=…`). A Greenhouse or Lever posting adds that ATS's documented notes to the advice, as `--ats` does, unless `--ats` names another. The CLI asks only the API host listed for the posting's host (`boards-api.greenhouse.io`, `api.lever.co`, `api.eu.lever.co`, `api.ashbyhq.com`), never the host in the URL; it takes `https` addresses only, follows no redirect, waits at most 20 seconds and reads at most 20 MB. A posting on any other site, or on Greenhouse's EU boards (which have no public API), is refused with a message to save the page and pass it with `--job`; `--job` and `--job-url` together are refused. The engine's core, `/job`, `/node` and the MCP server still make no network calls, and scores and recovered fields are the same for every input.
- ea72dfd: **Breaking:** a resume with a UK phone number (+44), a French resume, and a resume in a language with no pack are now read differently, so their recovered fields and scores change for the same input.

  - **A French language pack (`fr`) and a France region (`FR`)**, in `BUILT_IN_LOCALES` and exported from `/locales`. A French CV is read with its headings (with and without accents: "Expérience professionnelle", "Competences", "Centres d'intérêt"), months and their abbreviations ("janv.", "févr."), "depuis", "aujourd'hui" and "à ce jour", ranges by "à" and "au", level words ("langue maternelle" C2, "courant" and "bilingue" C1, "notions" A2), licence, diplôme d'ingénieur and doctorat, title and school words, French injection phrases, and a posting's "Missions", "Profil recherché" and "Les plus". `FR` reads day-first dates and the French system's credentials (brevet, baccalauréat, CAP, BTS, DUT, BUT, Bac+2/+3/+5/+8) and does not judge a date of birth or a photo, as a French CV commonly carries both. A French resume was read with English rules: on our fixtures it missed most section headings, read a degree line as a job and recovered no skills; it now reads every field. Both are `community` until a native-speaking maintainer reviews them.
  - **A United Kingdom region (`GB`).** A resume with a UK phone number (+44; not one the phone metadata places in Guernsey, Jersey or the Isle of Man, which names no region) now reads all-numeric dates day first ("01/09/2019" is September 2019, where it was January), GCSEs and O-levels (level 2), AS-levels and Highers (3), HND, HNC and foundation degrees (5), PGCE and postgraduate diplomas (7) and Welsh "Coleg" schools, and weighs a stated date of birth or a photo as a warning, as the US region does (it was a light note with no region). A-levels and degree classes ("2:1", "First-class honours") read as before. `report.locale.region` is `"GB"` for such a resume, where it was `null`.
  - **A language with no pack is no longer judged as English.** The policy now names its own language's common words (`text.detectionWords`) and those of eight languages it has no vocabulary for and thirteen scripts (`text.otherLanguages`), told by the same thresholds as a pack. A resume no attached pack recognises, written in one of those and not in English (a Spanish or Italian one, or a German one under the policy without packs), drops the rules limited to English (the eight writing checks) instead of passing or failing them on English words; its score moves by those rules. Another language is told only by the words a resume has, and only when it has more of them than of English, never by the English it lacks: a short or terse English resume with none of another language's words, or with fewer of them than English ones ("El Paso", "Banque Nationale du Canada"), is read as before. A resume with more of a pack's words than English ones, yet clearly English too (a French summary over English roles), is read with the pack's words but keeps the English rules, and its dates are not read as the pack's country writes them. `report.locale` keeps its shape. Both fields are new in the policy schema, with defaults, so a policy written before them parses unchanged.
  - **A resume's bullets decide which language it is read in.** A pack's vocabulary still attaches on three of its words at 3%, as before. When the resume's bullet lines hold more English words (`text.detectionWords`) than the pack's, it keeps month-first dates and the English writing rules: an English resume naming French or German institutions ("Banque Nationale du Canada", "Müller und Söhne") or opening with a French or German summary is read so, with the pack's words attached (`locale.languages` lists the pack, `region` is null). Before, such a resume took the pack's country and its day-first dates. A German or French CV with English headings or an English summary keeps its country, as before; a script pack (Hindi) decides as before.
  - **A degree is read only where a word ends, in any script.** The community policy's degree patterns ended before an ASCII letter only, so the "ma" of "Maîtrise de React" was a master's: a French posting asked for a master's degree and lost the skill line. They now end before any letter, so the policy's fingerprint changes.
  - **A baccalauréat named for its field is a bachelor's.** Québec's "Baccalauréat en informatique" (or "Bac en génie logiciel") reads at level 6 with the French pack, not as France's school diploma, and "Bac+2/3/5/8" is read by the French pack too, so a French posting asking for "Bac+5" is an education requirement under any region.
  - Bundle sizes (gzipped): `/locales` from 71.4 to 75.6 KB, `/ai` by 0.6 (to 73.0 with this release's redaction), `.` from 100.2 to 101.0, and `withLocales` alone from 48.1 to 48.7.

### Patch Changes

- b0c0c7f: Tighter limits on what a file or a resume can cost, and on what the AI analysis sends. Scores and recovered fields are the same for every resume a person would upload.

  - **A PDF's images are decoded a page at a time.** pdf.js decodes every image in full, about 12 bytes a pixel, and went on after the file had been read, all pages at once. The table pass now decodes no image, and each page waits (up to 2 s an image) for its own images before the next is read: six pages with a 48 MP photo each went from 2.3 GB to under 0.5 GB. There is still no size cap on an image: a 420 KB file with one 144 MP image holds 1.8 GB. Some images still decode after `extractResume` returns (in tiling patterns and Type3 glyphs, soft masks of any size, a page whose images take over 2 s), and a page with many large images decodes them all at once. The wait costs time: 60 pages with a 49 MP image each take 31 to 34 seconds, where the call returned in under half a second and left them decoding. Run extraction in `/node/child` with a timeout, and cap its memory in the operating system (a cgroup, `ulimit -v`, a Windows Job object): image buffers live outside the V8 heap, so `--max-old-space-size` does not bound them.
  - **`readJobFile` reads a posting only from a `.txt`, `.md`, `.html` (`.htm`), `.pdf` or `.docx` file**, and refuses any other with `AtsFileError` before opening it, as `readResumeFile` refuses an unknown resume type. A posting's words come back as missing keywords, so a credentials file or a key named as the posting (`ats-engine check --job`, the MCP server's `job_path`) was echoed back. A JSON file that does not parse is refused as "not valid JSON", with the line and column but without the parser's message, which quoted the file's text.
  - **PDF reading stops after the first 100 pages** as well as at the character cap: 5,000 empty pages held extraction for 11 seconds and 50,000 for nine minutes; they now take about half a second and two and a half. `pageCount` still counts every page.
  - **A text file's bytes that are not UTF-8 are decoded in one pass**: 20 MB of them took 37 seconds and now take under one. The text is the same for every input.
  - **A DOCX's page headers and footers share one 2 MB budget**, in name order; a part past it is neither read into the text nor measured. Each was read up to 8 MB, as many as the archive held: seven of 7.5 MB from a 163 KB file took nine seconds, now under half of one.
  - **`analyze` redacts more phone numbers and two-character names.** Any run of 9 or more digits on one line that opens with `+` or a trunk `0` (`07912 345678`, `020 7946 0958`, `(02) 9876 5432`) is replaced whether the parser read it or not, so a local number is redacted under a policy without its country's region; dates are not, one or a range or a list of ranges, in brackets or with a short note after them (`01/2020 - 12/2023`, `06/15/2019 – 08/30/2021`, `(01/2020 - 12/2023)`, `01/2020 - 12/2023 (3 yrs)`, `09/2019 - 06/2021 / 07/2021 - 12/2023`). So is a second North American number (`Home: (415) 555-0199`, `415-555-0199`). Each gets its own placeholder (`[PHONE_1]`, `[PHONE_2]`), restored in the reply. A name of two Chinese or Korean characters (`李明`) is replaced too, where it stands apart (on its own line, after a colon or a space); inside a Chinese sentence (`李明是工程师`) or before a Korean particle (`김민은`) it is still sent, as replacement is whole-word. Still sent: a number with none of these shapes, such as India's `98765 43210` unless its region pack is attached, which the README's AI sample now does.

## 0.9.0

### Minor Changes

- 3b17f9a: **Breaking:** a policy from `parseAtsPolicy` or `withLocales` is now frozen, all the way down, and so are `DEFAULT_POLICY`, the localised policy `localizePolicy` returns, and every other object the package exports (the locale packs `de`, `hi`, `US`, `DE`, `IN` and `BUILT_IN_LOCALES`, `atsLanguagePackJsonSchema`, `atsRegionPackJsonSchema`, `CONVERT_GROUNDING_SKIP`, `DOCUMENT_LIMITS`, `VERDICT_BANDS` and `/format`'s labels and bands).
